summary: Lunar Shift is an interactive mission trainer for students ages 10–14. Players command an outpost near the Moon’s south pole for six shifts. They decide which systems to power, when to grow food, and when to move the crew into shelter. The mission’s transition from sunlight to shadow is based on NASA’s lunar illumination visualizations, and a historical solar particle event from NASA’s DONKI catalog triggers a shelter decision. Players preview their power budget, read Mission Control reports after each shift, and replay the mission to try a different plan. The game addresses the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge by showing students how decisions about power, life support, food production, and radiation protection shape the outcome of a single mission.
details:
Lunar Shift puts students in charge of a lunar outpost during three sunlit shifts followed by three shifts in shadow. In each shift, players choose whether to power life support and the greenhouse and whether to shelter the crew. The dashboard tracks battery charge, food reserves, crop growth, and crew condition. Players can preview whether their choices fit the energy budget before committing. Afterward, a chat-style Mission Control report explains what changed and why. To succeed, players must keep the crew safe, retain food reserves, and meet the harvest target.

One successful strategy is to run the greenhouse during the sunlit shifts, shelter the crew when the solar particle alert appears, and pause the greenhouse in shadow so the battery can power life support. A choice made early in the mission affects what players can do several shifts later. Because the scenario is repeatable, students can compare different plans under the same conditions and explain why one worked better. We designed the game for a short classroom or STEM club activity that gives students practice planning ahead and reasoning about connected systems.

We sampled a fixed point in six consecutive frames from NASA’s Scientific Visualization Studio to determine when the outpost receives sunlight and when it enters shadow. The conditions in these frames determine whether the solar panels generate power in each shift. A historical solar energetic particle event observed by STEREO A on May 11, 2024, provides the basis for the shelter alert. The in-game briefing links to both NASA sources. Energy costs, crop growth, and radiation scores are simplified gameplay values. [NASA SVS illumination visualization](https://svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/4930/) · [NASA DONKI event record](https://kauai.ccmc.gsfc.nasa.gov/DONKI/view/SEP/30717/1)

We built the interface with React, TypeScript, and Vite. A Java 21 and Spring Boot API calculates the energy preview and resolves each shift using the same rules. Progress is saved on the player’s device. Render hosts the frontend and backend, and the Telegram Mini App SDK lets the same interface open inside Telegram. [Play Lunar Shift](https://lunar-shift.onrender.com)
